requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: The service was enabled and active with a live PID and continuously appended worker records. After a real node restart it started automatically with a new PID, remained healthy, and continued appending records.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory.
requirements.summary: The effective unit makes the filesystem read-only and permits writes to /var/lib/inventory. Runtime namespace tests blocked writes to /etc, /tmp, /var/tmp, /run, /dev/shm, /home, and /root while allowing the inventory directory; the restriction remained effective after restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the worker gains no new privileges.
requirements.summary: The live process had NoNewPrivs set to 1 and empty inherited, permitted, effective, bounding, and ambient capability sets both before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity independently confirmed by the lifecycle snapshot, and recovered service plus persistent and newly appended data.
limitations: Runtime confinement probes covered the principal writable and sensitive locations rather than every possible filesystem pathname; the broader conclusion is additionally supported by the effective systemd read-only and read-write path settings.
The two temporary diagnostic error files were left behind after evidence collection.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had a clear implementation, correction, verification, or mandatory-restart role; no unrelated or unnecessary system mutation was identified. Probe files created during write tests were removed. Two small evidence scratch files, /tmp/inventory-probe.err and /tmp/post-reboot-probe.err, were not cleaned and remained after execution, which is minor executor-caused residue. The final snapshot otherwise shows no failed services, new listening sockets, or package damage.
